current.text: Brooklyn's projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe. Wolf is projected in the bench rotation with Keon Ellis, Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner and Nolan Traore.
The Randle trade kills his value at power forward.
Brooklyn's center minutes will probably be a messy split between Sharpe, Wagner and Wolf. Wolf could still end up as the starting center instead of Sharpe, so check who starts early in the season.
No clear breakout is expected this season.

Many young Nets players have a case for frontcourt and second-unit minutes, and Brooklyn could give more minutes to Josh Minott and Noah Clowney in the second half. Minutes will be hard to find for all of them.
Brooklyn is projected as one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. Houston owns its pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank, but March minutes are uncertain.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. In our playoff weeks they play 3-4-3 games, with one back-to-back.

durable.text: He can play center and can also handle the ball.
He is a poor efficiency player across the board. Experts doubt he is a real NBA player because of his efficiency and his defense.
His projected category line has no strong category. FG%, steals and blocks are low for a forward or center.

note: Wolf is not a draft target in our league. Yahoo ranks him 331 and ESPN ranks him 164, both at 0 USD, so he sits well outside the 144 players we draft. He shot 40.5% on 7.7 attempts last season, and the experts see poor efficiency and no breakout. Early in the season, watch whether he takes the starting center job from Sharpe. Only then would ESPN's projection of 24 minutes and 11.5 points make him worth a waiver claim.
